terms.comment: No ancient or modern source has a word. Traupman’s dulciolum (not in Lewis & Short), fixed on the end of a little stick: praefīgō is to fix one thing on the end of another (Lewis & Short). In context dulciolum alone will do.
Not in Lewis & Short, and we have no other source for it; apparently formed on Greek λείχειν, “to lick”, which would give the long ī.

phrases.english: Lick your lollipop; don’t bite it.

sources: Lewis & Short: bacillum · Lewis & Short: praefigo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 286. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio has the heading “lollipop, sucker” with no Latin; Levi–Bini has no word.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
